rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage is reported to have been revealed about Saʿlaba ibn Hatib; after the Prophet warned him that little faithfully paid is better than much he could not bear, Saʿlaba renewed his request and vowed to give every rights-holder their due.
rows.anchor: Bunun da Sa‘lebe b. Hâtıb sebebiyle nâzil olduğu mervîdir. Şöyle ki Sa‘lebe Peygamber’in huzûruna gelmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿlaba's flock multiplied until Medina could not contain it; he moved to a valley and stopped attending the congregation and Friday prayer.
rows.anchor: derken üredikçe üremiş Medine dar gelir olmuş, bir vâdiye gitmiş ve cemaat ve cumadan kesilmiş.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Prophet's collectors asked Saʿlaba for the prescribed alms, he called them like the jizya and said he would think about paying, illustrating the withholding and turning away.
rows.anchor: Sa‘lebe’ye uğrayıp Resûlullah’ın ferâizi mübeyyin fermanını okuyarak sadakayı istediklerinde “bu cizyeler ne? Bunlar cizyenin kardeşi, hele siz gidin de düşüneyim” demiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the collectors returned, the Prophet twice lamented Saʿlaba before they spoke, and these verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: Tahsildarlar[^1] dönüp Resûlullah’a geldiklerinde daha onlar bir şey söylemeden iki kere يَا وَيْحَ ثـَعْلَبَة buyurmuş, bu sebeple bu âyetler nâzil olmuş.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afterward Saʿlaba brought the alms, but the Prophet refused it; Abu Bakr and Umar also refused it, and Saʿlaba died in Uthman's time, when the judgment of 9:77 had come to pass.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ebû Bekir’e getirmiş kabul etmemiş, Hazret-i Ömer’e getirmiş kabul etmemiş ve Hazret-i Osman zamanında helâk olmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their sirr is what they conceal in their hearts, while their najwa is their whispered conversation; God knows both.
rows.anchor: muhakkak Allah sırlarını: kalblerinde gizlediklerini ve fısıltılarını bilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes the hypocrites: should they not know that God knows the unseen, before daring to commit such acts against Him?
rows.anchor: Yani bunu bilmediler mi ki Allah’a karşı o haltlara cür’et ettiler?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Bedouin hypocrites around Medina belong to the Juhayna, Muzayna, Aslam, Ashjaʿ, and Ghifar tribes, which camped near the city.
rows.anchor: Cüheyne, Müzeyne, Eslem, Eşca‘, Gıfâr aşiretleri Medine etrafına inerlerdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Medinan hypocrites had become hardened and practiced in hypocrisy, adept at concealment and evading suspicion.
rows.anchor: Medine ahâlisinden de bunlar {مَرَدُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلنِّفَاقِ} münafıklıkta temerrüd etmiş yani sürtülmüş, mümarese peydâ etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You do not know them” means the Prophet could not identify their hypocrisy, not that he lacked their names, persons, or lineage; their concealment could defeat even his discernment until revelation came.
rows.anchor: şahıslarını, isimlerini, neseblerini bilmez değil, münafık olduklarını bilmezsin.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two punishments are punishment in this world and in the grave; the great punishment is eternal punishment in the Fire at resurrection.
rows.anchor: biri dünya azâbı biri kabir azâbıdır {ثُمَّ يُرَدُّونَ إِلَىٰ عَذَابٍ عَظِيمٍۢ} sonra da azîm bir azâba reddolunacaklardır ki bu da kıyamette müebbeden azâb-ı nârdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the other absentees, this group did not invent excuses: they admitted the wrong of missing the expedition without excuse, regretted it, and confessed honestly.
rows.anchor: öbürleri gibi yalandan mazeretlerle i‘tizâra kalkışmadılar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their good and bad deeds were mixed: they had gone on some expeditions and missed others, sinned, then regretted and acknowledged their sins.
rows.anchor: fena amel de yaptılar iyi[^2] de; meselâ gazâya gittikleri de oldu gitmedikleri de.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some of those who had stayed behind tied themselves to the mosque pillars and swore they would not untie themselves until the Prophet did; he also waited for a command, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: mütehallifler hakkında nâzil olan âyetleri işittiklerinde kendilerini Mescid-i Saâdet’in üstüvânelerine bağlamışlardı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once released, they offered their property for alms and purification; the Prophet said he had not been ordered to take anything from them, after which this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm da “emvâlinizden bir şey almakla emrolunmadım” buyurdu. Ba‘dehu şu âyet nâzil oldu:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alms cleanse them of the stains of sin and increase their good deeds, raising them to the rank of the sincere.
rows.anchor: günah lekelerinden temizlenmelerine ve hasenâtlarının tenmiyesiyle muhlisler derecesine terfî‘lerine sebep olasın.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking مِن as partitive, Elmalılı reports that the Prophet took one third of their property, not all of it.
rows.anchor: mallarının hepsini değil مِنْ أَمْوَٰلِهِمْ kaydındaki teb‘îza mürâ‘ât ederek üçte birini ahz eyledi denilmiştir.

rows.speaker: Hasen-i Basrî
rows.claim: Hasan al-Basri says this is a special, voluntary expiation for sins, not obligatory zakat or a financial penalty; it depends on willingness and intention.
rows.anchor: Hasen-i Basrî’nin kavli budur. Ma‘amâfîh bir cezâ-yı mâlî mâhiyetinde değil, tav‘u niyete mütevakkıf bir sadaka olmak üzeredir.

rows.speaker: ekser-i fukahâ
rows.claim: Most jurists take the command to concern obligatory zakat: the passage addresses the wealthy, love of wealth caused the sin, and willingly paying their due zakat would demonstrate sincere repentance and remove hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: Fakat ekser-i fukahâ demişlerdir ki bundan asıl murad farz olan zekâttır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı favors the obligatory-zakat reading while allowing extra voluntary gifts; on the alternative reading, the command requires the Prophet to take and accept expiatory alms, and thus more clearly applies to obligatory zakat.
rows.anchor: farz olan zekâtların ahz ve kabûlüne evleviyetle delâlet edeceği derkârdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's statement that he was not ordered to take their property may concern the refusal to accept alms from some, such as Hatib ibn Saʿlaba.
rows.anchor: “emrolunmadım” buyurmasının da Hâtıb b. Sa‘lebe gibi [2613] birtakımlarının sadakalarının kabûlünden memnû‘iyet meselesiyle alâkası muhtemildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet could not take charity for himself: obligatory alms were forbidden to the Prophet's family, and both obligatory and voluntary charity were forbidden to him.
rows.anchor: Âl-i Resûl fukarâsının sadakāt-ı vâcibeyi kabul etmeleri haram olduğu gibi Resûlullah’a vâcib ve tetavvu‘her sadaka haram idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's collection under the cited hadith was in his capacity as imam, who must collect and distribute alms; the verse establishes this duty and connects to the collectors of 9:60.
rows.anchor: bu âyet her hâlde sadakātın ahzında imamın bir vazifesi bulunduğuna delâlet eder ki وَٱلْعَٰمِلِينَ عَلَيْهَا [et-Tevbe 9/60] bununla alâkadardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted legal discussion says collecting alms belongs to the imam; a payer's direct payment to the poor does not suffice because the imam's right to collect remains.
rows.anchor: Bu âyet delâlet eder ki sadakātı ahz, imama aittir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet sent collectors for livestock and ordered them to take alms at the animals' locations and watering places.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem mevâşî sadakātına âmiller gönderir ve onlara mevâşînin mevzilerinde, sular üzerinde sadakalarının ahzını emrederdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's condition to the Thaqif delegation that they would not be assembled or tithed meant they need not bring livestock to collectors; collectors would visit watering and likely grazing places to collect.
rows.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm’ın Sakif vefdine بأن لا يحشروا ولا يعشروا diye şart etmesinin de mânası budur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same collection procedure applies to zakat on crops and fruit.
rows.anchor: Kezâlik sadakāt-ı simâr (hububat ve meyve) de böyle olacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakat on hidden assets was brought to the Prophet and the first caliphs, Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman.
rows.anchor: Diğer zekât-ı emvâl -yani emvâl-i bâtıne- ise Resûlullah’a ve Ebû Bekir’e ve Ömer’e ve Osman’a götürülürdü.

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: Uthman announced in Ramadan that debt should be paid first and the remaining wealth purified with zakat; he then left payment to the poor to each person's choice, ending the imam's collection right through a binding act of a just imam.
rows.anchor: ‘Bu ay zekâtlarınız ayıdır. Her kimin üzerinde deyni varsa te’diye etsin, sonra da bakıyye-i malını tezkiye eylesin’ dedi ve binâen‘aleyh mesâkîne edâsını [2614] herkesin kendisine bıraktı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uthman's policy was a valid agreement made by a just imam, binding on the community and therefore ending the imam's collection right in that case.
rows.anchor: Çünkü bu, eimme-i adlden bir imamın akdeylediği bir akiddir. Ve binâen‘aleyh ümmet üzerine nâfizdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Collectors were not sent for hidden wealth because it was concealed in protected homes and shops, agents could not enter them, and owners could not be compelled to produce all their assets; owners brought this zakat and their declarations were accepted.
rows.anchor: öyle emvâl-i bâtıne zekâtlarına sâ‘î gönderilmemiş idi, imama kendileri getirirler ve bu babda kavilleri makbul olurdu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When hidden assets circulated between towns as trade and became visible, collectors were appointed to take their zakat, as with livestock.
rows.anchor: bu emvâl, beldeden beldeye sevk ile tasarruf olunup mevâşî gibi zâhire çıktığı zaman bunlarda vâcib olan zekâtı ahzetmek için de âmiller nasbolunmuştur.

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz instructed collectors to take half a dinar per twenty from Muslim trade goods and one dinar per twenty from dhimmi goods, only after a year, citing a report traced to someone who heard the rule from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: Nitekim Ömer b. Abdülaziz müslimin[^15] mürur ettirdiği ticârâttan her yirmi dinarda yarım dinar, zimmînin geçirdiğinden her yirmi dinarda bir dinar alınmasını

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar ibn al-Khattab had earlier instructed collectors to take a quarter-tithe from Muslims, a half-tithe from dhimmis, and a full tithe from those at war with the Muslims.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer b. el-Hattab âmillerine müslimden rub‘-i öşür, zimmîden nısf-ı öşür, harbîden öşür almalarını yazmış idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Muslims, collection is obligatory zakat and requires the conditions of a completed year, nisab, and valid ownership; if zakat is not due, nothing is taken.
rows.anchor: müslimden alınan zekât-ı vâcibe olup bunda havl ve nisâb[^16] ve sıhhat-i milk gibi şerâit-i vücub muteber olur, eğer zekât vâcib değilse alınmazdı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umar's practice followed the Prophet's collection of livestock, fruits, and crops; because trade goods circulated openly in Muslim lands and no Companion objected, the rule became consensus, which Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz also followed with the cited hadith.
rows.anchor: Ashabdan bir kimse de buna itiraz ve muhalefet etmemiş binâen‘aleyh bir icmâ‘olmuştu. Ve işte Ömer b. Abdülaziz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means deferred for God's decision; irjāʾ means delay, and the Murjiʾa were so called for withholding a definitive judgment about whether repentance would be accepted.
rows.anchor: أرجيته veyahut أرجأته’den إرجاء tehir etmek demektir ki tevbenin kabûlüne kat‘iyyen hükmetmeyenlere “mürci’e” ıtlak olunması bundandır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مُرْجَوْنَ is the underlying form; Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Abu Bakr from Asim, and Yaqub read it with hamza as مُرْجَئُونَ.
rows.anchor: İbn Kesîr, Ebû Amr, İbn Âmir, Âsım’dan Ebû Bekir ve Ya‘kūb kıraatlerinde hemze ile مُرْجَئُونَ okunur.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the deferred group as Kaʿb ibn Malik, Murara ibn Rabiʿ, and Hilal ibn Umayya.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan rivayet olunduğuna göre bunlar Ka‘b b. Mâlik ve Murâre b. Rebî‘ve Hilâl b. Ümeyye idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike Abu Lubaba and the pillar-bound companions who promptly showed remorse, these men delayed their repentance; although they were participants at Badr, the Prophet suspended judgment and forbade greetings and conversation, while people disputed whether they were doomed or might be forgiven.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah bunların hükmünü tevkif eylemiş ve ashâbını onlarla selâm ve kelâmdan nehy eylemişti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may punish them if they persist in their condition or accept their repentance if they sincerely repent; His knowledge and wisdom govern both the deferral and what follows.
rows.anchor: Ya Allah bunları ta‘zîb edecek eğer bulundukları [2616] hâlde kalırlarsa {وَإِمَّا يَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِمْ} veya tevbelerini kabul eyleyecektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud's people say he brought no clear proof, refuse to abandon their idols at his word, and refuse to believe him.
rows.anchor: Ve biz senin sözünden dolayı ilâhlarımızı terk etmeyiz. {وَمَا نَحْنُ لَكَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ} Biz sana inanmayız.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people accuse their idols of having struck Hud with an evil that made him mad because he insulted them.
rows.anchor: ilâhlarımızdan bazısı her hâlde seni bir fenalıkla çarpmış yani onlara dil uzattığından dolayı aklına fenalık getirmiş, delirtmiş.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their “some of our gods” reflects their assigning different specialties and invented names to individual idols, each as a god of some particular matter.
rows.anchor: “Bazısı” demeleri putlarının her birine başka hâssa isnad ettiklerinden; şu filan husûsun ilâhı, şu falan husûsun ilâhı gibi isimler uydurduklarından dolayıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud answers their denial and rant by pointing to himself as one of the greatest divine proofs and asking God to witness.
rows.anchor: bizzat kendisinin[^1] en büyük beyyinât-ı ilâhiyeden olduğunu anlatan şu hakikatlerle cevap vererek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud calls them to witness that he is wholly innocent of the partners they have invented besides God.
rows.anchor: siz de şâhid olunuz ki {أَنِّى بَرِىٓءٌۭ مِّمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦ} onun gayrısından sizin uydurduğunuz şeriklerden ben kat‘iyyen berîyim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud challenges all the people and all their idols to scheme against him at once, without delay, asking what clearer proof of his confidence could be given.
rows.anchor: Yani bundan daha açık ne beyyine arıyorsunuz, yalnız bana fenalık getirdiğini iddia ettiğiniz bazısı değil bütün şerikleriniz ve siz hepiniz toplanarak bana fenalık yapmak için dilediğiniz planı kurun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud relies on God's command and protection: God is lord and master of both Hud and his people, so nothing they do or any harm that reaches him occurs apart from God's will.
rows.anchor: Ben her hâlde Allah’a tevekkül ettim O’nun emr ü hıfzına dayandım {رَبِّى وَرَبِّكُم} ki Rabbim ve Rabbinizdir. Benim de mâlikim, efendim O’dur sizin de.

words: مَّا مِن دَآبَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ ءَاخِذٌۢ بِنَاصِيَتِهَآ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every moving creature is in God's grasp and power, owned and subdued by Him; taking it by the forelock is an idiom for control and subjugation, and none escapes His disposal.
rows.anchor: Nâsıyesinden tutmak, perçeminden yakalamak, zabt u teshirde[^3] meseldir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is on a straight path in the sense that He upholds truth and helps the truthful; His pleasure lies with truth, justice, and uprightness.
rows.anchor: Doğruluğun hâmîsi, doğruların yardımcısıdır. Rızâsı hakk u adl ve istikāmettedir.

words: فَقَدْ أَبْلَغْتُكُم مَّآ أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِۦٓ إِلَيْكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the people turn away from these clear truths and the path of monotheism, Hud has fulfilled his duty by delivering what he was sent with.
rows.anchor: ben size gönderildiğim şeyi iblâğ[^4] ettim vazifemi yaptım

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may destroy them, replace them with another people, and give them succession; their rejection cannot harm God, and its harm falls on themselves.
rows.anchor: Yani sizi helâk eder, yerinize başka bir kavmi halef yapar, hilâfeti onlara verir

words: إِنَّ رَبِّى عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ حَفِيظٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God watches and preserves everything, nothing escapes Him, and the people's actions are not hidden; He can punish them without any possibility of their harming Him.
rows.anchor: Rabbim her şeyin üzerinde nâzır ve nigehbândır hiçbir şeyi kaçırmaz ve yaptıklarınız O’ndan gizli kalmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the account of the she-camel as God's sign, Elmalılı directs the reader to Surah al-Shuʿara.
rows.anchor: {نَاقَةُ ٱللَّهِ لَكُمْ الآية} Sûre-i Şu‘arâ’ya bak.
